edges.effect_quant: Pooled meta-analytic evidence point in more than one direction, so no single pooled effect estimate is reliable enough to summarize cleanly.
edges.mechanism: The proposed pathway combines changes in oxidative damage, inflammatory tone, hormone signaling, bile-acid metabolism, and exposure to food-derived carcinogens or protective phytochemicals. For Prostate cancer, those pathways matter over years, so consistent long-term intake patterns are more informative than short interventions.
edges.summary: Green tea appears tied to mixed effects on prostate cancer in adult men mainly through pooled meta-analytic evidence. The likely magnitude is modest, which is why the edge is framed conservatively rather than as a headline-level breakthrough.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.

evidence.citation: PerlettiG et al 2019 Arch Ital Urol Androl
evidence.notes: Green tea catechins for chemoprevention of prostate cancer in patients with histologically-proven HG-PIN or ASAP. Concise review and meta-analysis.
